chapterTitle: Lesson 1A – Present perfect simple and continuous

stems: Choose the correct option: Oh no, I ___ the bus! (the bus has gone)
questions.explanation: Present perfect simple – czynność zakończona, ważny jest skutek (autobus odjechał).
questions.sourceExcerpt: Grammar bank 1A: Oh no, I've missed the bus! (The bus has gone, so the action is completed.)

stems: Choose the correct option: I ___ Mandarin for two years, and I still have a lot to learn.
questions.explanation: Present perfect continuous – czynność niezakończona, wciąż trwa.
questions.sourceExcerpt: Grammar bank 1A: I've been learning Mandarin. (I'm still learning, so the action is not completed.)

stems: Choose the correct option: How long ___ Jessica?
questions.explanation: Know to czasownik stanu (state verb) – z nim present perfect simple, nie continuous.
questions.sourceExcerpt: Grammar bank 1A: How long have you known Jessica?

stems: Choose the correct option: I ___ this car since 2009.
questions.explanation: Own – czasownik stanu: present perfect simple dla stanu trwającego od przeszłości do teraz.
questions.sourceExcerpt: Grammar bank 1A: I've owned this car since 2009.

stems: Choose the correct option: We ___ for over forty minutes now!
questions.explanation: How long? + czynność długotrwała (wait) – present perfect continuous.
questions.sourceExcerpt: Grammar bank 1A: We've been waiting for over forty minutes now!

stems: Choose the correct option: We ___ more than 100 applicants so far.
questions.explanation: How many? – liczymy rezultat: present perfect simple.
questions.sourceExcerpt: Grammar bank 1A: We've interviewed more than 100 applicants. (How many?)

stems: Choose the correct option: He ___ €1,000 for charity.
questions.explanation: How much? – rezultat w liczbach: present perfect simple.
questions.sourceExcerpt: Grammar bank 1A: He's raised €1,000 for charity. (How much?)

stems: Choose the correct option: He ___ on that bench since this morning.
questions.explanation: Czasowniki długich czynności (sit, stand, wait, stay) + since – present perfect continuous.
questions.sourceExcerpt: Grammar bank 1A: He's been sitting on that bench since this morning.

stems: Choose the correct option: She ___ to speak to you all day – call her back!
questions.explanation: Czynność wciąż trwa (jeszcze z tobą nie rozmawiała) – present perfect continuous.
questions.sourceExcerpt: Grammar bank 1A: She's been trying to speak to you. (She still hasn't spoken to you, so she's still trying.)

stems: Choose the correct option: I'm afraid she ___ the office – she isn't here now.
questions.explanation: Czynność zakończona ze skutkiem teraz – present perfect simple.
questions.sourceExcerpt: Grammar bank 1A: I'm afraid she's left the office. (She isn't here now, so the action is completed.)

stems: Choose the correct option: He ___ to work – he always goes by bike.
questions.explanation: Doświadczenia i nawyki z always/ever/never – present perfect simple.
questions.sourceExcerpt: Grammar bank 1A: He's never driven to work, he always goes by bike.

stems: Choose the correct option: I ___ my own bread – I never buy it.
questions.sourceExcerpt: Grammar bank 1A: I've always baked my own bread.

stems: Which sentence focuses on the RESULT of the activity?
correct: He's passed all of his exams.
distractors: He's been studying for his exams.
He's been working on his essay.
He's been preparing for the test.
questions.explanation: Simple – skupienie na rezultacie; continuous – na samej czynności.
questions.sourceExcerpt: Grammar bank 1A: He's passed all of his exams. (Focuses on the result) / He's been studying for his exams. (Focuses on the activity)

stems: The present perfect continuous is used mainly to:
correct: focus on the activity itself and its duration
distractors: focus on the result of a completed activity
talk about states with verbs like know or own
describe a finished action at a definite past time
talk about experiences with ever and never
questions.explanation: Continuous: czynność sama w sobie, How long?, powtarzanie, długie czynności.
questions.sourceExcerpt: Grammar bank 1A: We use the present perfect continuous to focus on the activity itself … to answer the question: 'How long?'

stems: In which sentence is there NO important difference between the two forms?
correct: Mauro has lived / has been living in Bologna since 2010.
distractors: I've missed / I've been missing the bus.
I've known / been knowing Jessica for years.
He's passed / been passing all his exams.
I've owned / been owning this car since 2009.
He's driven / been driving 3,000 km in total.
questions.explanation: Z work, live, study obie formy znaczą praktycznie to samo.
questions.sourceExcerpt: Grammar bank 1A: Sometimes there is no important difference … with verbs such as work, live and study. Mauro has lived/has been living in Bologna since 2010.

stems: Choose the correct option: They ___ over 3,000 kilometres this month.
questions.explanation: How far? – rezultat (odległość): present perfect simple.
questions.sourceExcerpt: Grammar bank 1A: They've driven over 3,000 kilometres. (How far?)

stems: Which verb is a state verb, normally NOT used in the present perfect continuous?
questions.explanation: Czasowniki stanu (know, own, like, believe, understand) – bez form ciągłych.
questions.sourceExcerpt: Grammar bank 1A: We use the present perfect simple, NOT the present perfect continuous, with state verbs

stems: Choose the correct option: Your eyes are red. ___ ?
questions.explanation: Widoczny skutek trwającej czynności – present perfect continuous.
questions.sourceExcerpt: Grammar bank 1A: We use the present perfect continuous to focus on the activity itself.
